description: Assesses the appropriate identity and access management strategy based on service type, user base, data sensitivity, and integration requirements.

recommendation.pattern: Managed Identity Service with Federated Authentication
recommendation.rationale: Public-facing services with large user bases require a scalable identity solution that supports self-service registration, password reset, and multi-factor authentication. Managed identity services handle the complexity of secure credential storage, brute-force protection, and compliance with accessibility standards.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Requires understanding of OAuth2/OIDC flows; managed service handles credential storage and MFA infrastructure
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: MFA policy updates, federation trust management, user lifecycle management, and security event monitoring

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Per-active-user pricing; MFA adds per-authentication cost; scales with user base
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: User migration; application integration; MFA rollout; user communication

recommendation.rationale: Internal services handling sensitive data should integrate with the organisation's enterprise directory (typically Active Directory or Azure AD) and enforce conditional access policies. This ensures consistent identity governance, device compliance checks, and risk-based authentication.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Requires identity team collaboration; conditional access policies need security team input
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Access reviews, conditional access policy updates, group membership management, and privileged access monitoring

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Enterprise directory licensing (often already in place); conditional access features may require premium tier
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: Application integration with enterprise SSO; conditional access policy design; user training

recommendation.rationale: API services require machine-to-machine authentication using OAuth2 client credentials or API keys with proper lifecycle management. This provides secure, auditable access control for service-to-service communication without user interaction.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Standard development team can manage OAuth2 flows; API key rotation needs automation
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Key rotation, scope reviews, client credential lifecycle management, and usage monitoring

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Minimal additional cost; typically included in API gateway or identity service pricing
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: OAuth2 implementation; client onboarding process; documentation

recommendation.pattern: Privileged Access Management with Hardware MFA
recommendation.rationale: Systems handling SECRET or TOP SECRET data require privileged access management with hardware-based multi-factor authentication, just-in-time access provisioning, and comprehensive audit trails. Access must be time-limited and require explicit approval workflows.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Requires dedicated security operations team; approval workflows need management oversight
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Hardware token lifecycle, access certification campaigns, session recording review, and policy updates

costConsiderations.runningCosts: PAM platform licensing; hardware token costs; security operations staffing
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: PAM platform deployment; hardware token procurement and distribution; process design

recommendation.rationale: Without cloud access, identity management relies on on-premises Active Directory with Active Directory Federation Services for SSO. This provides enterprise authentication but requires more infrastructure management than cloud-based alternatives.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Requires dedicated Active Directory administrators; domain controller management
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: Domain controller patching, replication monitoring, certificate renewal, and group policy management

costConsiderations.runningCosts: Windows Server licensing; hardware for domain controllers; staffing
costConsiderations.transitionCosts: AD design and deployment; ADFS configuration; application integration

defaultRecommendation.rationale: When no specific conditions strongly favour an alternative, a managed identity service with single sign-on provides secure, scalable authentication with minimal operational overhead. This supports both user and service authentication with built-in MFA capabilities.

operationalBurden.staffingImplications: Standard development team can integrate; managed service handles infrastructure
operationalBurden.ongoingMaintenance: User lifecycle management and policy reviews

commonQuestions: Who are the users and how will they authenticate?
Is there an existing enterprise directory to integrate with?
What level of MFA is required for the data classification?
What is the user lifecycle management process?
Are there requirements for GOV.UK One Login integration?
evidenceNeeded: Data classification and corresponding access control requirements
MFA requirements based on risk assessment
artefactsToProduce: Identity and access management decision record (ADR)
